elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2 now reads "Kubient hereby grants to Customer and, upon written notice to Kubient, its affiliates a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive ... license". "Customer" is defined at p0000 as The Associated Press alone, so the affiliate extension adds new coverage rather than duplicating it. Note the grant runs directly from Kubient to the affiliates, so it is not a Customer transfer of access to a third party.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The revised grant names only "Customer and ... its affiliates"; no words such as "and contractors acting on its behalf" appear anywhere in § 2, and no sublicense right exists ("without right of sublicense" retained). To meet this element the drafter must add contractors acting on Customer's behalf to the list of licensees in § 2.

§ 2 grants a "limited, royalty-free" licence with no term characterisation; nothing states that a paid-up licence is perpetual, and the licence remains tied to the Services/Agreement term (with revocation on termination noted at p0021). An express "perpetual with respect to paid-up licences" statement is required.

The word "revocable" is expressly retained in the rendered grant ("without right of sublicense, revocable license"). Irrevocability would require deleting "revocable" and adding "irrevocable" for paid-up licences; the drafter consciously left this to the preferred level.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No termination-of-licence standard was inserted; the licence stays "revocable" on its face with no limitation to uncured material breach. Add operative words limiting revocation/termination of the licence to Customer's uncured material breach.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The rendered grant deletes "non-transferable, non-assignable" and inserts "transferable to Customer's successor in a merger or acquisition without Kubient's approval", consistent with the § 14(h) assignment carve-out. It is limited to M&A successors rather than successors generally, which is noted but not fatal to this element.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "grants to Customer and, upon written notice to Kubient, its affiliates" — coverage is conditioned on written notice exactly as the fallback contemplates, and affiliates are not already within the defined term "Customer" (p0000 names only The Associated Press), so there is no duplicate coverage.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: The blocking words "non-transferable, non-assignable" are removed and replaced with an express, unconditional permission: "transferable to Customer's successor in a merger or acquisition without Kubient's approval". This aligns with the retained § 14(h) permission to assign without consent to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, so no contradiction remains.

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete: both elements are implemented in operative text of § 2 (affiliate coverage on written notice; express M&A-successor transferability without Kubient's approval). The claimed target level is therefore achieved and the "deviation" finding is correct, because the original § 2 was expressly "non-transferable, non-assignable" and ran to The Associated Press alone.

Preferred remains incomplete on four elements: contractors acting on Customer's behalf are still excluded, "revocable" is retained (defeating irrevocability), there is no perpetuity statement for paid-up licences, and there is no limitation of licence termination to uncured material breach. These are correctly left unpressed as preferred-only points.

Minimality holds. The only deletions are "non-transferable, non-assignable", which directly contradict the selected transferability element and had to go; the Customer-favourable "royalty-free", "non-exclusive" and "without right of sublicense" terms, the purpose limitation, and the Google Ad Manager mechanics are all retained untouched. Using a direct "without Kubient's approval" transfer permission rather than a notwithstanding override of § 14(h) is the correct minimal device, and no survival tails, expense language or extra procedures were added.

Intent is preserved: § 14(h) (which already allows assignment without consent to an affiliate or M&A successor) now reads consistently with § 2 instead of being overridden by the specific "non-transferable" licence term; no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is left dangling.

Residual risk to close in negotiation (not a defect in the elements): the rationale asserts that § 6(a) bars third-party access without Kubient's prior written approval. Because the new grant runs directly from Kubient to the affiliates rather than through a Customer transfer, § 6(a) should not bite, but a short conforming carve-out ("except as permitted under Section 2") would remove any argument. Do not add it unless Kubient raises the point, as it would be an extra outside the fallback checklist.

Also note for the comment, not the redline: the effects-of-termination revocation at p0021 mis-cites "section 3"; leaving it unamended is correct at the fallback level since irrevocability sits only at preferred.
